title: GDR-HGNN: A Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks Accelerator Frontend with Graph Decoupling and Recoupling
problem: Irregular memory access patterns in Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks cause buffer thrashing in HGNN accelerators, significantly limiting performance and throughput.
motivation: Heterogeneous GNNs are important for graph representation learning, but practical hardware acceleration is hindered by memory access inefficiencies.
method: GDR-HGNN eliminates buffer thrashing—when the cache becomes overwhelmed with scattered memory requests—by splitting heterogeneous graphs (graphs with multiple types of nodes and edges) into regular subgraphs with predictable, sequential memory access. The accelerator processes each regular subgraph more efficiently because the cache can reuse data it's already loaded, then recouples the results to reconstruct the correct output. This transforms the graph's natural irregularity into a structured access pattern the hardware can optimize.
key_novelty: By splitting heterogeneous graphs into regular subgraphs and recombining results, GDR-HGNN restructures memory access to eliminate buffer thrashing in HGNN accelerators.
contributions: Novel graph decoupling and recoupling technique to eliminate buffer thrashing in HGNN accelerators
HGNN accelerator frontend architecture with improved memory efficiency for heterogeneous graphs
Evaluation demonstrating performance improvements over existing HGNN acceleration approaches
limitations: Specific evaluation scope, scaling characteristics to very large graphs, and applicability to other heterogeneous structures not discussed.
